intent: Compare COVID-19 vaccination rates among Black, White, and Hispanic U.S. adults from February through August 2021.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
How do COVID-19 vaccination rates among Black, White, and Hispanic U.S. adults compare from February through August 2021?
From February to August 2021, the vaccination rate among White U.S. adults increased from 21% to 72%.
From February to August 2021, the vaccination rate among Hispanic U.S. adults increased from 16% to 76%.

units.claim: All 4 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: From February to August 2021, the vaccination rate among Black U.S. adults increased from 15% to 70%.
units.computation: Compare first and last values for Black series: 15% (Feb '21) to 70% (Aug '21); intermediate June '21 value is 60%.
accept: Black vaccination rate rose from 15% in Feb '21 to 70% in Aug '21
Black series shows an upward trend over the period

units.claim: From February to August 2021, the vaccination rate among White U.S. adults increased from 21% to 72%.
units.computation: Compare first and last values for White series: 21% (Feb '21) to 72% (Aug '21); intermediate June '21 value is 65%.
accept: White vaccination rate rose from 21% in Feb '21 to 72% in Aug '21
White series shows an upward trend over the period

units.claim: From February to August 2021, the vaccination rate among Hispanic U.S. adults increased from 16% to 76%.
units.computation: Compare first and last values for Hispanic series: 16% (Feb '21) to 76% (Aug '21); intermediate June '21 value is 68%.
accept: Hispanic vaccination rate rose from 16% in Feb '21 to 76% in Aug '21
Hispanic series shows an upward trend over the period

optional_valid: Asian* series is present in the chart but not explicitly requested in the intent; it may be shown but is not required for the comparison.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for differences in vaccination rates
Comparisons involving the Asian* series as a required element
review_notes: The intent asks to compare three groups (Black, White, Hispanic) over time; each group's trend is a separate semantic unit because the comparison is across entities, not a single cross-panel comparison.
The Asian* series is present in the data but not part of the requested comparison; it should not be required.
No crossing or threshold units are needed because the intent does not ask for them and the data do not show crossings among the three requested groups.
